d: The Prince of Bouillon, the Abbot of Chazeuil and sayings. The left door opens. The Prince solemnly enters, followed by Chazeuil.

Adriana and the sayings. Adriana Lecouvreur, in the eastern costume of "Rossana" enters from the last exit on the right, with the scroll of her part between her hands. The other actresses turn their backs spitefully; the Prince and the Abbot bow; Michonnet contemplates her ecstatic. She does not notice anyone, staying at the end of the room.
Michonnet and Adriana
Adriana and Maurizio.
The Prince, the Abbot; then M.lla Dangeville and M.lla Jouvenot. The Prince enters from the left, the Abbot from the bottom of the right.
M.lla Jouvenot, M.lla Dangeville, Quinault, Poisson, then Michonnet.
Michonnet
Maurizio, Michonnet, then Quinault; then M.lla Jouvenot. Maurizio comes back upset by the first left exit, while Michonnet follows to rumble in all the furniture of the hall.
All less Maurizio.
Maurizio and said. Maurizio of Saxony enters from the fund.
The Prince, the Abbot and Maurizio.
Adriana and sayings.
Adriana and Maurizio.
The Abbot, Michonnet and sayings.
Adriana, Maurizio and the Abbot.
Michonnet, Adriana and Abbot. Michonnet gets weird.
Adriana and Michonnet

Adriana, then the Princess. Adriana blows out, one by one, all the candles of the doubles; the living room remains faintly illuminated by the lunar light, filtering from the windows. She remains a still, unresolved moment, facing the door of the toilet.
The Abbot with various small valleys. Some small valleys have chairs at right distance; others lower curtains; others carry large vases of flowers and ornamental plants.
The Princess, the Abbot and the servants. The Princess of Bouillon, dressed in great gala, enters from the first exit on the right.
The Abbot and the Princess.
The Prince, Dame, Lords and sayings. The Prince in a ceremonial dress enters from the left, while introduced by the Butler enter subsequently from the door of the bottom Dame, Knights, etc.
The butler, then Adriana, Michonnet and sayings.
The butler, then Maurizio and sayings.

The dancing fun. Two valleys raise the veil of the theater, marked on the sides by ornamental scenes and at the top by garlands of flowers: the background represents a classic landscape with the sea in the distance. Paride in dress of Pastor Frigio, resting over a poget of Verzura. A matte of Amorini weaves, around the dull, a carola. At the soft sound of pastoral instruments, distant voices accompany the puerile dances.
Michonnet and the waitress. Michonnet comes in from the starboard, followed by the waitress, who points to the bedroom door.
Adriana and Michonnet. Adriana in white bathrobe appears on the bottom door and stops at the threshold.
La Jouvenot, la Dangeville, Quinault, Poisson and sayings. At the last words of the two, the four Comédie members enter from the door of the anteroom.

The waitress and sayings. Everyone abandons themselves to gaiety. The waitress returns carrying a tray over which is a hood covered in crimson velvet, to which is tied with ribbons a note. Adriana gets up and goes to get him. The others continue to madness, except Michonnet slowly following Adriana.
Michonnet and Adriana.
Adriana and Maurizio. Maurizio enters anxiously. At the first seeing him Adriana runs to meet him throbbing: then he repents, and Ristà.
The waitress and sayings. The waitress comes in from the bedroom and looks dismayed.
